answer: Stop sybils with a velvet queue, a summit audit, and an oasis cut. Every identity enters through a velvet queue: a sponsor locks a bond, and the k-th identity one sponsor backs costs k squared, so N clones pay about N cubed. Newcomers earn weight only by surviving surprise summit audits, where a rotating panel of seasoned agents tests behavioral independence. Rewards come from a shared oasis, and each identity's draw is capped by the min-cut of the endorsement graph around it, so clones behind one sponsor split one thin cut. One failed audit burns the sponsor's whole velvet bond.
